parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment targets a specific, identifiable component of the paper: the baseline comparison in the experimental evaluation, which is limited to only ICL and zero-shot approaches. While it does not explicitly name a section, table, or figure, the baselines are standardly located in the experimental setup/results section, so it is obvious to the authors which part the comment addresses. Under the rubric, grounding is satisfied when the addressed part is explicitly mentioned or obvious to the authors, so the grounding requirement at the top level is met. Moreover, the comment is specific: it clearly identifies the issue (missing RAG-based and long-context baselines) and suggests concrete improvements. Therefore, the comment is both grounded and specific, satisfying the criteria for the highest grounding and specificity level.
